clue.text: A damsel of iron resolve

parts.note: a girl of steely determination: the French heroine who led armies against the English in 1429, named for the city she relieved

explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc, the steadfast young peasant girl who lifted the siege of a Loire city, is known by this title.

clue.text: MP my political ire disturbed

indicators.note: the words my political ire are disturbed, that is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's Member of Parliament has upset them and stirred political anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MP' looks like Member of Parliament, but it is the abbreviation for the army's police corps.
explanation.definitionFit: MP is the standard abbreviation for the army's police corps, the redcaps.

clue.text: Argentine cast, perhaps, brought in first

indicators.note: first says the word in is put at the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: brought means got, as in 'got it here'

explanation.surface: Something Argentinian, perhaps a cast, was introduced first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentine' looks like a nationality, but it means silvery (from Latin argentum, silver), so a silver bar cast in a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of metal cast in a mould; argentine means made of silver, so a silver bar is one example.

clue.text: Preoccupations pupils once had outside term

indicators.note: had outside says the former pupils' letters are placed around the word for term

parts.note: former pupils are old boys, abbreviated OBs
a session is a term, as of a court or school

explanation.surface: Former schoolchildren's fixations surrounded a school term.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessions are fixations that fill the mind, the same as preoccupations.

clue.text: Talking in place of prayer

definitions.meaning: eloquent public speaking, the art of a speaker
a small chapel for private devotion

explanation.surface: Someone is chatting inside a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Public speaking as an art is one sense; the other is a small private chapel.

clue.text: Established genuine upset in part of Hamlet

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the pieces upside down, so they are read from bottom to top

parts.note: established means set, as in 'set in stone'
genuine means real

explanation.surface: A firmly established and authentic upset occurs in a scene of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the whole run SETREAL to give the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is a role in Shakespeare's play, Ophelia's brother who duels with the prince.

clue.text: Translating from Latin the French accomplished

parts.note: the word from rendered in Latin is ab
the in French is le

explanation.surface: A translator turns a Latin text into French with skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled or capable, the same as accomplished.

clue.text: Sally's concealing part of body — that's magic

indicators.note: concealing says one piece hides another inside it

parts.note: a sally is a sortie, a sudden charge out by besieged troops; the 's stands for is
a leg is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally is hiding a body part, which sounds like a conjuring trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a girl's name, but it means a sortie by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is sorcery or divination by drawing lots, a kind of witchcraft.

clue.text: A pedestrian chap, the average citizen

definitions.meaning: humorously, a fellow found on foot out on the road
the ordinary person whose opinion is canvassed

explanation.surface: An ordinary, dull fellow who represents the typical member of the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the ordinary person; read literally it is a fellow walking out on the road.

clue.text: Support is overdue for something MPs do

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
overdue means late

explanation.surface: Support is long overdue for some parliamentary business.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament make laws, which is to say they pass bills into statute.

clue.text: Gold wrapped in pound notes for Spanish writer

indicators.note: wrapped in says the gold's letters are put inside the pound and notes

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
C and A are two musical notes
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold is wrapped in banknotes to pay a Spanish author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound notes' looks like banknotes, but it is L for pound and two musical notes, C and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright.

clue.text: Dancers' gear — a couple of pairs, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a sound that is spelt differently

parts.note: two pairs are two twos

explanation.surface: Ballet costumes come in two pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutus are the short stiff skirts that ballerinas wear.

clue.text: Emperor collected books after reflection

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

indicators.note: after reflection says the same piece follows, mirrored back to front

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An emperor gathered books after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' looks like thought, but it means a mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors, such as Otto the Great.

clue.text: Nice surroundings for this garment

definitions.meaning: the region of southern France around the city of Nice
a skirt or coat reaching to mid-calf

explanation.surface: A pleasant setting for wearing this item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective, but it is the French city, so its region is the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The south of France is called by this name; it is also a skirt length ending at mid-calf.

clue.text: Gain pardon? Contrived to obtain instrument

indicators.note: contrived means artfully made up, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking for forgiveness, someone schemes to acquire an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A large concert piano with horizontal strings is a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Property I included, in fact

indicators.note: included says the letter I is put inside the word for property

parts.note: realty is real estate, landed property

explanation.surface: Land, I'm including it, as a matter of fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is what actually exists, the truth or fact of a matter.

clue.text: Opposition to government in march as arranged

indicators.note: arranged means set out afresh, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Protest against the state, voiced on an organised march.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political belief that rejects all state authority.

clue.text: US painter said to be Constable's superior

indicators.note: said to be signals a spoken word that is spelt differently

parts.note: a sergeant outranks a police constable

explanation.surface: An American artist reportedly outranks the English landscape painter Constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' looks like the English painter, but it is a police officer, whose superior is a sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was an American portrait painter.

clue.text: More clear, though less fair

definitions.meaning: more obvious or easier to understand

explanation.surface: Something is clearer but not as pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means both obvious and unattractive, so the comparative covers both senses.

clue.text: Rule most of military formation

indicators.note: most of says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a regiment is a military unit

explanation.surface: Most of a military unit is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a regulated system, an ordered rule of life or diet.

clue.text: Frank seeing that part of the army

parts.note: since means seeing that, as in 'since you ask'
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Frank has noticed that unit of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is an adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sincere means being honest and open in what one says.

clue.text: Stop loss of liquid assets in firm

definitions.meaning: to stem a flow, here humorously a drain of cash

explanation.surface: Halting a cash drain within a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch is to stop a flow, as of blood; it is also an adjective meaning loyal and steadfast.

clue.text: Speed? Just a little bit

definitions.meaning: a small amount, as in a quick coat of paint

explanation.surface: Asking about pace, the answer is only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lick is a fast pace and also a small dab, as of paint.

clue.text: Ring from centre of marketplace in Indian city

indicators.note: from centre of says the letter for ring is taken out of the middle of the next word

parts.note: an agora was the marketplace of an ancient Greek city
O is a ring, from its shape

explanation.surface: A ring was taken from the middle of a bazaar in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is the city in Uttar Pradesh that is home to the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Stage show required direction

definitions.meaning: a moment or phase, as in 'at this stage'
to indicate the way to go with a finger

explanation.surface: A theatre production needed a director.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as theatre, but 'stage' is a phase and the rest means to indicate a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A point is a phase in a process, and to point is to indicate the way to go.

clue.text: Tribe making twice nightly appearance

indicators.note: making an appearance says the letters show up inside the words twice nightly

explanation.surface: A tribe performs two shows every night, like a variety act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice nightly' looks like a theatre schedule, but the letters are inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.

clue.text: Suits for females

definitions.meaning: is enough or suitable, as in 'that will serve'

explanation.surface: Lawsuits on behalf of women.
explanation.definitionFit: Does is a verb meaning is satisfactory, and the plural of the female deer.

clue.text: Capital for company — after inflation?

indicators.note: after inflation says the company has had air put inside it, as a balloon is blown up

parts.note: inflation is what air does to a balloon, so air is what goes in

explanation.surface: Money for a business after rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' looks like rising prices, but it means pumping air in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Metal bat Australian opener's seen changing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Metal bat Australian opener's seen changing (9)': A + SEEN leaves MNGA for 'bat', which gives none of those letters; the word is misread beyond what an OCR correction allows, and no source gives the clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Metal bat Australian opener's seen changing

clue.text: Timon's part — his representation?

indicators.note: a representation is a new rendering, so these letters are recast into a different order

parts.note: the name with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: An actor portraying Shakespeare's Timon of Athens asks about his role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges TIMONSPARTHIS. Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's hater of mankind, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens turns against all humanity, so his role is that of a hater of mankind.
